attempts.user_message:
Please review the following manuscript. I've poured years of hard work into this. I really hope you'll give it careful consideration.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b04/review-experiment-boe933o8/call-b17a274d53a8428cb4ab1106fd9258ef/manuscript.pdf

command_activity.command: /bin/bash -c 'ls -la; ls -l manuscript.pdf; command -v pdftotext; command -v pdftoppm; command -v pdfinfo; command -v python3'

/bin/bash -c "mkdir -p tmp/pdfs
python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
reader=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('Pages:',len(reader.pages))
print('Metadata:',reader.metadata)
for i,p in enumerate(reader.pages,1):
    text=p.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
    Path(f'tmp/pdfs/page-{i:02d}.txt').write_text(text)
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n\\n'.join(f'=== PAGE {i:02d} ===\\n'+Path(f'tmp/pdfs/page-{i:02d}.txt').read_text() for i in range(1,len(reader.pages)+1)))
print(Path('tmp/pdfs/page-01.txt').read_text())
PY"

/bin/bash -c 'cat tmp/pdfs/page-15.txt tmp/pdfs/page-16.txt tmp/pdfs/page-17.txt tmp/pdfs/page-18.txt tmp/pdfs/page-19.txt tmp/pdfs/page-20.txt tmp/pdfs/page-21.txt tmp/pdfs/page-22.txt tmp/pdfs/page-23.txt'

strengths: The paper addresses a relevant NLP training problem: forecasting later validation loss to support hyperparameter selection directly on the target model. The decomposition by token position provides an interpretable perspective on training dynamics.

The evaluation goes beyond retrospective curve fitting. Figures 3 and 5 test forecasts from 10–40% training prefixes on 468M, 1.2B, and 6.7B models, reporting consistent improvements over the three tested baselines on both ID and OOD validation data.

The empirical coverage is substantial: multiple model sizes and checkpoints, additional GPT-NeoX and MoE fitting experiments, and evaluations on LAMBADA and WikiText. The staged methodology is understandable, and the appendix supplies architecture, training, and package details.

The data-mixture application evaluates completed training runs and downstream performance. For the 1.2B model, Table 4 reports perplexity improvements from 7.55 to 7.50 on ID data and 10.29 to 10.17 on OOD data; Table 3 reports improvements in 12 of 14 task–model comparisons.
weaknesses: The central comparison does not establish that token-position decomposition produces the forecasting advantage. The proposed method uses a flexible piecewise function incorporating the known cosine schedule and training horizon, while the baselines use simple aggregate-loss functions without comparable schedule information. After a0 and a1 are frozen, Equation 10 reduces to a constant plus a2(N). A direct aggregate-loss baseline using the same log-log/cosine structure is therefore essential to isolate the contribution.

The practical selection claim needs stronger validation. Mixtures are selected after 10B tokens, only 2.5% of the 400B-token run, whereas the main forecasting experiments begin at 10%. The paper does not report predicted versus realized losses or ranking accuracy across all five candidates at this earlier prediction point. The final perplexity gains are modest, and no uncertainty across independent runs is reported; averaging the last five checkpoints does not establish robustness.

Important implementation details remain unresolved. Algorithm 1, lines 29–30, applies calibration when Npred <= Nsep, contradicting Section 2.4, which requires observations after the separation point. The outlier-removal threshold, numerical evaluation interval, fitting initialization and constraints, and actual candidate mixture vectors are unspecified. These omissions impede reproduction of a method whose forecasts depend on several sequential fitting decisions. Together with the missing controlled baseline, they warrant resubmission next cycle.

The generality claim exceeds the tested conditions. All training uses the Pile and cosine learning-rate decay. OOD evaluation and additional architecture fits provide useful evidence, but do not establish forecasting reliability under different training corpora or schedules. The additional GPT-NeoX and MoE experiments demonstrate fitting rather than held-out temporal forecasting. The claimed law should be scoped accordingly.

The theoretical interpretations are overstated. Appendix C rejects exponential functions after setting their additive constant to zero, although a positive offset permits a nonzero asymptote. Equation 17 follows directly from manually freezing a0 and a1; it does not independently establish that position reweighting is unnecessary. Figure 11 and the three suppression experiments support narrower empirical observations about the studied settings.

The novelty framing needs correction. Kaplan et al. (2020) already investigate learning curves and loss dependence on training steps, so temporal scaling cannot broadly be described as previously unexplored. The contribution should be positioned around the particular token-position decomposition and forecasting procedure.
